name: Basil
tile_uses: The tomato plate, toast, the vinaigrette
why_now: Basil is at its most fragrant in warm weather. July heat brings out the volatile oils. The best basil right now smells like summer itself.
how_to_choose: Bright, even green leaves — no dark spots
buy_this_much: One or two good bunches. It moves through a week faster than you expect.
buying_note: Using basil all month? A small potted plant may last longer than a cut bunch and lets you take only what you need. A cut bunch works well when you only need it once or twice.
price_note: Usually inexpensive — one of the least costly things in the basket.

flavor_paths.name: Torn, raw
flavor_paths.description: Over tomatoes, after the heat. The fragrance is the point.

flavor_paths.name: With peach
flavor_paths.description: A few leaves with a peach and flaky salt. Unexpected and very good.

flavor_paths.name: In the drink
flavor_paths.description: In place of mint in the spritz.

weekday_uses: Over shrimp and corn from the hot pan
In the spritz, instead of mint
weekend_use: Torn over the tomatoes and burrata, generously.
storage: Keep at room temperature with stems in water, like flowers. Do not refrigerate. Use within three or four days.
one_thing_to_learn: Tear basil instead of chopping when it will be served fresh. The knife bruises it and darkens it quickly. Torn leaves hold their color and fragrance longer.
